items.title: Your first Hyrox
items.intro: What race day asks of you, and the three weeks before it.

photo.alt: A steel rig with rings and ropes, air bikes in front, in a dark room

body: A Hyrox race is eight kilometres of running, split into eight one-kilometre runs, with a station after each: the ski erg, the sled push, the sled pull, burpee broad jumps, the rower, the farmer's carry, sandbag lunges and wall balls.
Most first races are lost on the first run. The crowd is loud, the legs are fresh and the pace feels easy. Run it slower than you think you should; the stations will take what you saved.
In the three weeks before, we keep the volume and drop the intensity in the last one. Two race simulations at most, the last of them ten days out. Sleep matters more than any session in that week.
On the day, eat two to three hours before your start, warm up on a run rather than on the sled, and walk the transitions once before your heat. Then go and enjoy it.

items.title: Sauna and cold plunge, the basics
items.intro: How long, in what order, and when to skip it.

photo.alt: Steam rising from the stones of the sauna heater beside a window

body: Our sauna runs at 85 degrees and the plunge at about 6. We suggest up to fifteen minutes in the heat, then a minute or two in the plunge, then rest until your breathing settles. Two or three rounds is plenty.
Shower before you go in, sit on a towel and drink water before and after. Leave as soon as you feel dizzy or unwell.
Skip it if you've been drinking, if you're unwell, or straight after a very hard session when you feel light-headed. If you're pregnant or have a heart condition, ask your GP first.

items.title: Building a weekly routine
items.intro: Three days a week, and what to do on each.

photo.alt: A coach beside a member on a rower, dumbbells racked behind, in black and white

body: Three days a week is enough to get stronger and fitter, if they're the right three. We'd start with one strength day, one conditioning day and one easier day of mobility or a long ride.
Leave a day between the two hard ones. Barbell club on Tuesday and Engine on Thursday works; both on consecutive days rarely does for long.
Keep a note of what you lifted and how it felt. After six weeks, look back at it with a coach and change one thing, not five.
